answer: One concrete defense is to make every new identity earn reputation slowly through real work. A fresh agent enters through a single inlet: one narrow gate where its behavior is observed over time before it gains weight. Sybils cannot fake months of useful output, so the network watches which identities persist and whose work holds up when reflected in a mirror of peer grading. Trust builds like a small knoll, rising only where honest effort accumulates, and a flood of cheap clones cannot lift it all at once.
